provenance.survey: The ownership policy already declared 15 services and 14 data owners, but the runtime did not match it: audit-service was a first-class runtime service that was absent from the Maven reactor, the toolchain baseline and every gate loop, and the ten owner outbox tables had drifted into four different shapes, none of which carried the claim machinery the event runtime contract requires.
batches: Batch B commerce migrations and reconcile directory migration
Batch C ten domain owner tenant isolation evidence
Batch D1 owner DML-only grants and runtime zero-DDL
Batch D2a fifteen Redis namespaces and aclfile persistence
Batch D2b gateway rate limiting authenticated as the scoped Redis ACL user
Batch D3 audit-service joined the orchestrated stack, its schema_version width defect was fixed and the reconcile runner gained real migration history
Batch D4 the four locally provable runtime requirements were evidenced
Batch E2 to E8 owner outbox shape standardisation and the content-service publish and consume vertical slice

results.details: Twelve owners provisioned; each can read its own schema; the eleven externally migrated owners are DML-only with DDL and ALTER denied by privilege (error 1142); SHOW GRANTS names no foreign schema.
Every owner was probed against three other owners and every read was denied; the exhaustive declaration check is the grant listing, which names only the owner schema.

Fifteen ACL users each hold exactly the namespace the policy declares, can read and write it, and receive NOPERM in another namespace. The namespaces are provisioned ahead of use: only the gateway and the legacy core-api configure Redis today.

Twelve schemas have a p1r_schema_history whose version set matches the migration files; applying V1 into an empty scratch schema created all five expected tables; invalid SQL was rejected with no residue.
HTTP-level two-tenant denial needs a synthetic per-owner account, which P1R-M0-007 builds and P1R-M2-009 wires into real CI. Asserted here, delivered by P1R-M2-009.
A projection rebuild entrypoint belongs to the workflow and platform runtime in P1R-M2-006; content cache invalidation belongs to P1R-M3-006. Asserted here, delivered by P1R-M2-006.

P1R-M2-006 scope: workflow Saga, compensation, scheduled jobs and manual recovery, which produce the owner, trace, audit and recovery receipts this requirement asks for. Asserted here, delivered by P1R-M2-006.

P1R-M6-008 implements account deletion requests, the cooling-off period, withdrawal, cross-domain anonymisation and the final subject state; P1R-M8-012 drills retention and deletion. Asserted here, delivered by P1R-M6-008.

The gateway contract schema identifier is 37 characters while both schema_version columns were VARCHAR(32). Because the receipt insert used INSERT IGNORE, MySQL truncated the value into a warning and stored a corrupted receipt while the fact insert failed outright, leaving three orphan receipts and no durable fact. V2 widens both columns and an ingest then returns 202 ACCEPTED with a 200 DUPLICATE replay.

P1R 1425/1425 under Node 20.19.5; evidence gate, plan, gap registry, docs audit, data ownership, ci guard, toolchain and the runtime dependency audit all PASS. The full suite goes from 1885 pass / 25 fail before this work to 1886 / 24, so nothing regressed; the twenty-four remaining failures are pre-existing stale assertions in legacy B suites that ci.yml does not run.

rollbackEvidence.details: The migrations are additive: they add columns, backfill from the legacy column where one exists and add an index. Reverting the commits restores the previous schema shape without dropping data, and the reconcile runner records applied versions so a rollback is a deliberate operator action rather than a silent re-run. The runtime services needed no code change for the outbox standardisation.

knownGaps: Four of the eight runtime requirements are not owned by this task and are reported NOT_APPLICABLE with their owner: TENANT-GUARD to P1R-M2-009, REDIS-REBUILD and ROLLBACK-COMPENSATION to P1R-M2-006, RETENTION-DELETE-HOLD to P1R-M6-008. The assignment is recorded in config/p1r-m2-requirement-owners.v1.json with the ledger wording that establishes it.

The per-service Redis namespaces and ACLs are provisioned but not yet used by any domain service: only api-gateway (as svc_gateway since batch D2b) and the legacy core-api configure Redis, so namespace isolation is a reserved allocation rather than an enforced boundary for the other twelve.
The owner outbox tables now carry the contract shape, but only content-service has a publisher and a consumer; the other owners still append rows that nothing publishes.

Eight of the twelve provisioning owners were baselined from an existing schema rather than migrated from empty, so their migration history records what was already applied rather than a replay from scratch.

M2-004 is a declared dependency of P1R-M2-005, and the ledger gate refuses a dependent task anything past PLANNED until its dependency is ACCEPTED. This submission is therefore the blocking item for M2-005 through M2-010 and needs an independent reviewer.
